clue.text: Mourns epic broadcast in part of theatre

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the two words before it are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grieves for a sweeping epic shown on air while sitting in a part of the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a television word, but it signals that MOURNS and EPIC are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: The proscenium is the arch and stage area in front of the curtain, a structural part of a theatre.

clue.text: Fish I displayed in position

indicators.note: displayed in tells us the letter I is set out inside the word for position

parts.note: a position is a place, as in 'take your place'

explanation.surface: A fish and the letter I are shown off in their proper position, like a museum exhibit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaice is a flatfish common in British waters, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Quiet after performing rugger forward surge

indicators.note: after tells us the word for quiet comes later, at the end

parts.note: an actor who is performing is on stage, so 'on'
RU is short for Rugby Union, which is called rugger in Britain
sh is the sound used to ask for quiet

explanation.surface: A rugby forward makes a quiet charge while playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rugger forward' reads as a player position, but 'forward' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An onrush is a sudden rush ahead, a synonym for a surge moving forward.

clue.text: Savoy perhaps with unusual end to Madame Butterfly

parts.note: Savoy is a variety of cabbage, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are set in an unusual, different order
end to picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A staging of Puccini's opera Madame Butterfly at London's Savoy, perhaps, with an unexpected ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' shuffles WITH plus E (the end of 'Madame') to WHITE. 'Madame Butterfly' looks like the opera title, but only 'Butterfly' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabbage white is a common pale butterfly whose caterpillars eat brassicas, an example of a butterfly.

clue.text: Clear visitor from the heavens appears in holy books

indicators.note: appears in tells us the visitor shows up inside the holy books

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a collection of holy books
ET is the alien visitor of the film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: An alien plainly turns up in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear profit is what is left after deductions, which is the meaning of nett, a spelling of net.

clue.text: Neglected racer found wandering

indicators.note: wandering means straying from place, so the letters of the two words before it stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A neglected racehorse is discovered roaming loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left uncared-for has been neglected, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bubbly essential for post-Christmas tipple

indicators.note: essential for says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fizzy wine is a must for a drink after the Christmas festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine, and bubbly is a casual name for any sparkling wine.

clue.text: Two types of fuel sent up to house the Queen in women's quarters

indicators.note: to house means the reversed fuels take the Queen in
sent up in a down clue means the fuel words are written bottom to top

parts.note: oil is one type of fuel
gas is the second type of fuel
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Fuel supplies are delivered upstairs to lodge the Queen in the harem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns OILGAS into SAGLIO, and 'to house' puts ER inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the secluded women's apartments in a Muslim palace, also called the harem.

clue.text: Appreciate batsman's position

definitions.meaning: to appreciate is to rise in value, as property does
in cricket a batsman is safe when in the crease, the marked line at the wicket

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits into IN CREASE: a cricket batsman behind the crease line cannot be run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets that appreciate grow in value, so the verb is a synonym; the cricket phrase describes where a safe batsman stands.

clue.text: Doing stunts on high bar, one caught cracking nuts

parts.note: Aero is a brand of chocolate bar

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so one and caught break into the word for nuts

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, nuts
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A gymnast performs tricks on the high bar, while a single catch splits some nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high bar' reads as gymnastics apparatus, but 'on high' ends the definition and 'bar' is the chocolate AERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobatics are stunt manoeuvres performed by aircraft in the sky, so doing stunts up high.

clue.text: Dishes half smashed? Little reptile!

indicators.note: half smashed means only the front half of the dishes word survives the breakage

parts.note: crockery is plates and dishes collectively

explanation.surface: A tipsy diner with broken plates spots a small lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half smashed' sounds like half-drunk, but it takes the first four of eight letters of CROCKERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Croc is the informal shortened name for a crocodile, so 'little' marks the abbreviation of the reptile.

clue.text: Smelly stuff gives fellow utter outrage

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
rank means utter or absolute, as in a rank outsider
to incense someone is to outrage them

explanation.surface: A man voices total fury about something that stinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' tempts as FRANK, a man's name, but it is only F; 'utter' is the adjective RANK, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankincense is an aromatic resin burned for its scent, so a jokey description of perfumed material.

clue.text: One with equal role upset actors

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the word after it are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer given equal billing has annoyed the rest of the cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-star shares top billing with another lead performer, an actor of equal standing.

clue.text: Stop meeting professional villain

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a rogue is a villain or scoundrel

explanation.surface: Someone tries to halt a gathering of a seasoned crook.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue parliament is to suspend its sessions without dissolving it, so to stop it meeting.

clue.text: Around start of concert there's more merit playing sensitive instrument

indicators.note: Around means the rearranged words go round the letter from the concert
playing means the letters are played about, rearranged
start of picks the opening letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: At the start of a concert there's extra talent on show from a delicate instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges the nine letters of the two words, and 'Around' wraps them about the concert's first letter; 'sensitive' is part of the definition, not a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A micrometer is a gauge measuring tiny lengths precisely, so an instrument sensitive to minute differences.

clue.text: Opted to work with incisor, as part of dentistry

indicators.note: to work means the letters are put to work, set into a different order

explanation.surface: A dentist chose to operate on a front tooth, as part of practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Periodontics is the branch of dentistry treating gums and the structures supporting teeth.

clue.text: Tooth present briefly in place where it should be

indicators.note: in tells us the short present goes inside the place word

parts.note: a socket is the hollow where a tooth belongs
pr is a short form of present, as in the grammatical tense

explanation.surface: A tooth is briefly back where it belongs, at a dentist's.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprocket is one of the projecting teeth on a wheel that engage a chain.

clue.text: Pack mainly containing revolt, warning things are too hot

indicators.note: containing means the shortened pack word holds the revolt word
mainly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to pack a case is to fill it
to rebel is to revolt

explanation.surface: A mob largely stuffed with insurrection gives an alarm that the situation is heating up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' cuts FILL to FIL, which holds REBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire bell is rung to warn of fire, a literal alarm that things have got too hot.

clue.text: Orchestra's man arranged main orch.

parts.note: Phil is a man's name

indicators.note: arranged means the following letters are set out in a new order, as music is arranged

parts.note: the abbreviation is taken as its letters

explanation.surface: A conductor has arranged a principal orchestral work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' reads as musical scoring, but it shuffles MAIN and ORCH into HARMONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Philharmonic is used as a name for a symphony orchestra, as in the London Philharmonic.

clue.text: Manage model party

parts.note: a make is a model or brand, as of a car
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cope with a fashion bash.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to manage or get by with what is available, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: We hear of Alfred and Alexander, perhaps, in scrapes

indicators.note: We hear says the following is about how something sounds when spoken

parts.note: Alfred the Great and Alexander the Great are examples of greats

explanation.surface: We learn of two famous kings caught in tight spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrapes' looks like a noun for trouble, but it is the verb, as a fork grates on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To grate is to rub harshly against something, so grates and scrapes are verb synonyms.

clue.text: Extra work performed in the long run

definitions.meaning: hours worked beyond the normal shift
read as two words, a game that has run beyond its normal length

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a sports one: a match that runs on has gone into extra time.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is hours worked beyond the usual schedule, and also play extended past the scheduled end.

clue.text: Sir Tim recalled eating the French cake

indicators.note: eating means the reversed name takes in the French article
recalled means called back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Sir Tim Rice is the lyricist of Evita and Jesus Christ Superstar
la is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: The lyricist remembered tucking into a French pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns RICE into ECIR, which takes in LA.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate, a kind of cake.

clue.text: Clear flirtatious move

definitions.meaning: to clear an exam or hurdle is to get through it successfully
to make a ... at someone is to make an advance

explanation.surface: An obvious attempt at romance.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a test is to clear it, and a pass is also an amorous advance.

clue.text: Look back and observe

indicators.note: back means the look word is read backwards

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: Someone is told to glance behind and watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look back' reads as a phrase, but 'back' reverses PEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a rule or promise is to observe it, a synonym in the sense of complying.

clue.text: People in a series of races have not commonly achieved goal

parts.note: the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is the series of motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: in tells us the people go inside the colloquial word

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of have not
men are people

explanation.surface: Competitors in a run of contests haven't, in slang, reached their target.
explanation.definitionFit: An attainment is something accomplished, so a goal that has been reached.

clue.text: Count as Swiss hero

definitions.meaning: to count, as a bank teller counts money
William, the legendary Swiss archer who shot an apple from his son's head

explanation.walkthrough: A teller in a bank is one who counts money.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell money is an old sense of to count it, and William of that surname is the Swiss folk hero.

clue.text: Shakespeare role American's doing well

parts.note: Prospero is the magician in The Tempest
US is short for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A US actor is thriving in a Shakespeare part.
explanation.definitionFit: To be prosperous is to be thriving or successful, so doing well.
